evidenceClaims.statement: Suspected adult blunt cardiac injury requires ECG and troponin I assessment; CK-MB does not replace either component.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline for the exact management rule; no universal assay cutoff or serial schedule.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

evidenceClaims.statement: A post-trauma ECG change or elevated troponin I supports cardiac monitoring; baseline ECG comparison matters.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single 2012 guideline; an abnormal screen does not identify a particular structural lesion.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

evidenceClaims.statement: Routine echocardiography is not the initial screening strategy for every hemodynamically stable blunt-chest-injury patient.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline; elevated biomarkers require monitoring and clinical reassessment, and new symptoms may change the imaging indication.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

evidenceClaims.statement: Cardiac CT or MRI may help distinguish traumatic cardiac injury from infarction in selected patients after initial evaluation.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Level 3 recommendation; not a substitute for the acute indicated bedside echocardiogram.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described outside-hospital trauma setting.

evidenceClaims.statement: Persistent new arrhythmia or hemodynamic instability after blunt chest trauma warrants echocardiography.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline; the related inadequate-TTE claim specifies when TEE follows. No routine TEE for every screened patient.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

evidenceClaims.statement: When echocardiography is indicated after blunt chest trauma but an adequate transthoracic study cannot be obtained, TEE is the supported next modality.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline. No esophageal contraindication or new imaging technology eligibility rule is invented.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described outside-hospital trauma setting.

evidenceClaims.statement: Normal ECG and troponin I remove the BCI monitoring indication in the EAST pathway without resolving other admission needs.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline; timing remains unsettled and this does not claim perfect universal diagnostic sensitivity.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

evidenceClaims.statement: A sternal fracture does not independently mandate cardiac monitoring when ECG and troponin I are normal.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline; other chest-injury needs remain.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

evidenceClaims.statement: Analgesia, coughing support and respiratory rehabilitation address impaired breathing after traumatic chest-wall injury.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single current guideline; no invented spirometry admission threshold, analgesic regimen or automatic level of care.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

evidenceClaims.statement: An inadvertently organ-traversing chest tube should stay in place pending urgent cross-sectional assessment and controlled multidisciplinary management.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single current guideline. No removal technique, exact vascular procedure, numeric stability threshold or new clinical probability is authored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described outside-hospital trauma setting.

verificationBySource.verificationRole: Targeted primary guidance; case observations constructed.

evidenceClaims.statement: Ongoing thoracic hemorrhage with hemodynamic instability warrants operative control even when drain output understates the blood loss.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Current and older society guidance agree that physiology outweighs output alone. Constructed drain observations are not new volume thresholds.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

evidenceClaims.statement: Unstable thoracic vascular bleeding favors open exploration, whereas suitable stable arterial injuries may permit endovascular treatment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single current guideline; no universal competition between all open/hybrid approaches or unverified device eligibility.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described outside-hospital trauma setting.

evidenceClaims.statement: Thoracoscopy can manage selected residual hemothorax or bleeding in a hemodynamically stable trauma patient.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline. This does not make VATS the appropriate first access during resuscitation-dependent shock.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described outside-hospital trauma setting.

evidenceClaims.statement: Substantial retained traumatic hemothorax after tube drainage favors early VATS over thrombolysis in an operative candidate.
evidenceClaims.limitation: EAST conditional, very-low-quality evidence, update in process. Exact early boundary in EAST is at most four days; draft supplies hospital day three without claiming a universal deadline.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

evidenceClaims.statement: Residual traumatic pleural blood can contribute to empyema and fibrothorax.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Older guideline used for the general complication relationship; no incidence, deadline or probability authored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described outside-hospital trauma setting.

evidenceClaims.statement: Persistent respiratory impairment with displaced rib injuries despite multimodal and regional analgesia supports considering rib stabilization.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Thresholds in PS 1.2 directly verified; draft uses multiple severely displaced ipsilateral ribs and failed ventilator liberation. Stabilization is a specialist assessment, not a guaranteed outcome.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

evidenceClaims.statement: Pulmonary contusion does not automatically exclude an otherwise appropriate patient from rib stabilization assessment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Individualized surgical assessment remains necessary; the draft does not treat contusion as evidence that fixation is automatically beneficial.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

evidenceClaims.statement: Tracheostomy may support prolonged ventilatory care but does not reconstruct displaced ribs.
evidenceClaims.limitation: The counterfactual describes treatment purpose, not an exact tracheostomy timing or automatic indication.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described outside-hospital trauma setting.

evidenceClaims.statement: Men age 65 through 75 who have ever smoked should receive one-time abdominal ultrasound screening for abdominal aortic aneurysm.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Exact pre-existing atomic statement and stable claim ID retained; source mapping freshly verified. Limited to asymptomatic previously unscreened men; not a diagnostic strategy for symptoms.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Asymptomatic men 65-75 with previous tobacco use and no completed abdominal aortic screen.

evidenceClaims.statement: A scan ending near the celiac origin does not assess the infrarenal abdominal aorta.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Underlying aortic segment relationships independently synthesized from the official anatomy/segment definitions; no figure copied.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Interpreting the inferior boundary of a thoracoabdominal acquisition.

evidenceClaims.statement: Symptoms attributable to an intact AAA warrant repair assessment regardless of usual asymptomatic diameter thresholds.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Pain attribution requires clinical assessment; no universal numeric pain or observation interval is supplied.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Symptomatic intact AAA.

evidenceClaims.statement: Attachment-site flow into an excluded sac represents a sealing failure.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Type I origin; one directly checked specialty standard.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Post-EVAR sac opacification.

evidenceClaims.statement: An established type I endoleak warrants prompt correction of the seal.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Cuff extension requires an available healthy landing segment; complex cases may need other repair. One directly checked publication.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Persistent or late attachment leak.

evidenceClaims.statement: An isolated type II endoleak with stable sac size can undergo imaging follow-up.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single publication; requires exclusion of higher-pressure leaks and continued surveillance.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Asymptomatic patients with stable post-EVAR sac.

evidenceClaims.statement: Retrograde flow from aortic side branches can fill the excluded sac.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Type II physiology; other inflow sources must be assessed.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Post-EVAR branch-associated flow.

evidenceClaims.statement: Sac enlargement with uncertain leak origin requires investigation for occult type I or III inflow.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Catheter angiography with possible cone-beam CT can resolve inconclusive CTA; no disputed growth cutoff is taught.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Enlarging post-EVAR sac.

evidenceClaims.statement: Ascending aortic involvement establishes type A dissection even with a distal entry tear.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Classification depends on extent, not simply the tear location.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Aortic dissection extending retrograde.

evidenceClaims.statement: Acute type A dissection requires emergency surgical evaluation and immediate repair.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single checked multisociety guideline. This draft does not rank contested mesenteric-first strategies.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Operable acute ascending dissection.

evidenceClaims.statement: Acute type B dissection with organ malperfusion warrants intervention, commonly TEVAR when suitable.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Static branch disease can require adjuncts; no automatic bowel resection or non-aneurysm ischemia objective is included.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Complicated acute type B dissection.

evidenceClaims.statement: Uncomplicated acute type B dissection initially receives medical therapy and close monitoring.
evidenceClaims.limitation: High-risk morphology and later complications can change the plan; does not ban elective later TEVAR.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Acute descending dissection without rupture or malperfusion.

evidenceClaims.statement: Use intravenous beta blockade first, adding intravenous vasodilation if pressure remains high.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single directly checked recommendation; contraindications can favor a non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker. No dose or numeric target is authored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Hypertensive acute aortic syndrome without beta-blocker contraindication.

evidenceClaims.statement: Acute aortic-syndrome therapy generally targets a heart rate of 60-80 beats per minute while maintaining organ perfusion.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single checked guideline; individual perfusion and contraindications govern treatment. No dose is taught.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Monitored hospital treatment of acute aortic syndrome.

evidenceClaims.statement: Intravenous nicardipine is an antihypertensive vasodilator that can be combined with beta blockade under monitoring.
evidenceClaims.limitation: The regulatory label verifies pharmacology; ACC/AHA establishes adding vasodilation after initial beta blockade when pressure remains uncontrolled. No dose or infusion-rate rule is authored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Hospital blood-pressure treatment after initial impulse control.

evidenceClaims.statement: An intravenous non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker is a reasonable acute aortic-syndrome rate-control alternative when beta blockers are contraindicated or not tolerated.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single checked guideline. This is a rate-control alternative, not evidence that switching from tolerated beta blockade is preferred for persistent pressure elevation after rate control.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Acute aortic syndrome with a beta-blocker contraindication or intolerance.

evidenceClaims.statement: Planned left-subclavian coverage should account for a patent LIMA coronary graft by preserving its inflow.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Elective setting with native landing zones; bypass versus transposition depends on anatomy.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: TEVAR involving LSA with LIMA-dependent myocardium.

evidenceClaims.statement: Carotid-subclavian transposition requires temporary proximal subclavian clamping.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single directly checked guideline; the anatomy-specific interruption matters for a pedicled LIMA.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Open subclavian transposition.

evidenceClaims.statement: A patent pedicled LIMA coronary graft favors bypass over subclavian transposition to avoid interrupting coronary inflow.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single directly checked guideline, section on LSA revascularization; other bypass/endovascular configurations remain specialist decisions.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: LSA revascularization with a patent pedicled LIMA.

evidenceClaims.statement: New spinal-cord dysfunction after TEVAR calls for perfusion rescue, including pressure support and CSF drainage assessment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Rapid specialist response; drainage contraindications must be checked. No invented target, timing, guaranteed recovery or routine prophylactic drain rule.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Post-TEVAR neurologic deficit.

evidenceClaims.statement: A small PAA with thrombus and distal embolic findings merits repair consideration despite being below 20 mm.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline, weak recommendation/low-quality evidence; excludes acutely threatened limbs requiring an ischemia-specific pathway.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: PAA under 20 mm with embolic findings.

evidenceClaims.statement: Finding a PAA warrants screening the opposite popliteal artery and abdominal aorta.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline, strong recommendation/moderate evidence; this is aneurysm screening, not broad asymptomatic arterial-stenosis screening.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Patients with a diagnosed PAA.

evidenceClaims.statement: Open repair is preferred for an intact TAAA requiring repair in Marfan syndrome.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single directly checked guideline; does not preclude endovascular rescue or exceptional high-risk situations. Newer ESVS full text was inaccessible.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Fit patient with heritable native-aorta TAAA.

evidenceClaims.statement: Unexplained infection or gastrointestinal bleeding after aortic grafting warrants cross-sectional graft evaluation.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline; imaging and cultures are interpreted together, and an unrevealing endoscopy does not assess the graft.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Prosthetic aortic graft with unexplained infection/bleeding.

evidenceClaims.statement: In an at-risk cirrhotic liver, a new solid lesion larger than 1 cm is characterized using dedicated multiphasic contrast CT or MRI.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One adequate newly retrieved publication supports this fact; no independent direct corroboration is claimed.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

evidenceClaims.statement: A suspicious lesion remaining uncharacterized after adequate dynamic imaging may require biopsy to establish tumor type before treatment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Supports persistent indeterminacy here, not routine biopsy of every lesion or of classic HCC imaging.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

evidenceClaims.statement: A subcentimeter nodule detected during HCC surveillance can follow close imaging surveillance rather than the immediate diagnostic pathway used for a larger solid lesion.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No exact surveillance interval is taught. Applies to the stated at-risk surveillance setting, without another supplied concerning finding.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

evidenceClaims.statement: In cirrhosis, a lesion at least 2 cm with nonrim arterial hyperenhancement and nonperipheral washout can satisfy an imaging diagnosis of HCC.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Applies to adequate multiphasic examinations in the appropriate at-risk population; no imaging diagnosis for an arbitrary noncirrhotic mass.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing multidisciplinary liver-tumor evaluation and major-hepatectomy planning.

evidenceClaims.statement: A malignant-appearing liver observation with rim arterial enhancement in an at-risk liver requires tissue classification because it is not specific for HCC.
evidenceClaims.limitation: AASLD recommends biopsy for LR-M observations; this is not a universal preoperative-biopsy rule for every suspected resectable cholangiocarcinoma.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing multidisciplinary liver-tumor evaluation and major-hepatectomy planning.

evidenceClaims.statement: Biopsy is not routinely required solely to establish the diagnosis of an imaging-characteristic HCC, although an independent tissue or molecular indication may justify sampling.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Multidisciplinary decisions can favor tissue even for LR-5 observations. The minimum-required-sampling task excludes a trial or separate molecular-tissue indication.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing multidisciplinary liver-tumor evaluation and major-hepatectomy planning.

evidenceClaims.statement: Solitary localized HCC with preserved hepatic reserve and no clinically significant portal hypertension supports specialist resection assessment when remnant and anatomy are favorable.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Cross-check of the existing favorable-profile claim. Portal hypertension is not asserted to prohibit every limited resection.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

evidenceClaims.statement: A hepatic resection plan must preserve sufficient functioning liver with arterial and portal inflow, hepatic venous outflow and biliary drainage.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Apply to the stated anatomy and care phase; patient-specific ranking requires clinical review.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

evidenceClaims.statement: Thermal ablation provides more reliable local control for small HCC than for progressively larger lesions.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Qualitative size-related suitability only; no universal procedure ranking or exact probability is taught.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

evidenceClaims.statement: For the approved profile of a solitary HCC with preserved liver function, no clinically significant portal hypertension, adequate future liver remnant, and no macrovascular invasion or extrahepatic disease, hospital HPB-surgery referral for hepatic resection evaluation is the selected disposition.
evidenceClaims.limitation: This is a deliberately favorable multiparametric profile, not a universal treatment rule for every solitary HCC or every person with Child-Pugh A cirrhosis. EASL 2025 metadata was not locally verifiable, so this package records the single-source limitation rather than inventing a second citation. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the owner-approved compensated-cirrhosis profiles in this package.

evidenceClaims.statement: Clinically significant portal hypertension is one selection consideration in the approved favorable resection profile.
evidenceClaims.limitation: This package does not teach clinically significant portal hypertension as an absolute contraindication to every limited hepatic resection, nor does it make preserved liver function alone sufficient for selection. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Learners applying only the clear favorable-profile boundary in the approved cases.

evidenceClaims.statement: Limited HCC burden with decompensated cirrhosis supports transplant-center assessment rather than assuming a routine favorable resection pathway.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Assessment is not guaranteed listing; one retrieved government summary directly corroborates the historical local decision.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

evidenceClaims.statement: Meeting standard Milan criteria supports transplant-center evaluation but does not by itself guarantee listing or transplantation; disease outside Milan criteria may still warrant specialist evaluation of other pathways.
evidenceClaims.limitation: This concept intentionally excludes AFP policy, downstaging selection, organ allocation, liver function, comorbid contraindications, and individualized treatment choice. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Learners applying standard Milan criteria without equating a tumor-burden classification with automatic listing or permanent exclusion.

evidenceClaims.statement: HCC commonly draws substantial arterial flow while surrounding liver depends importantly on portal flow; arterial embolization with major portal obstruction can endanger hepatic function.
evidenceClaims.limitation: NCI identifies portal-vein thrombosis as a relative TAE/TACE contraindication. This is not an absolute ban on every specialist-directed locoregional technique.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

evidenceClaims.statement: Advanced HCC outside a suitable locoregional pathway warrants medical-oncology assessment for systemic treatment when hepatic function and general condition permit.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No named systemic regimen, dose or first-line ranking is keyed. Current primary updates need targeted verification before such details are added.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

evidenceClaims.statement: Standard Milan classification requires no macrovascular invasion and no extrahepatic disease.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Microscopic pathology, transplant-center assessment, tumor biology, and other candidacy factors are outside this narrow recognition concept. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma whose staging is being compared with standard Milan criteria.

evidenceClaims.statement: TACE can be considered for nonmetastatic HCC unsuitable for surgery or ablation when hepatic perfusion and reserve permit.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Not a universal treatment hierarchy, a fixed tumor cutoff or an assertion that all portal obstruction permits routine TACE.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

evidenceClaims.statement: Borderline pancreatic cancer commonly requires neoadjuvant systemic treatment and restaging rather than immediate surgery.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Venous reconstructibility and local criteria require expert review. No universal neoadjuvant rule for clearly resectable disease is scored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

evidenceClaims.statement: Reconstructible portal/mesenteric venous involvement need not make pancreatic cancer permanently unresectable.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Independently synthesized guideline fact; exact application remains subject to named clinical review.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

evidenceClaims.statement: Distant metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma ordinarily calls for systemic treatment rather than curative pancreatic resection.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Exceptional oligometastatic research strategies are not a routine resection indication.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

evidenceClaims.statement: Obstructive jaundice before neoadjuvant therapy is an indication for biliary drainage; endoscopic covered metal stenting is preferred to plastic stenting in the verified consensus.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single directly verified ranking; no duration, bilirubin cutoff or metal-stent subtype superiority beyond that guidance is invented.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

evidenceClaims.statement: During pancreatic-cancer neoadjuvant therapy, metal biliary stents have lower recurrent obstruction and reintervention rates than plastic stents in comparative pooled evidence.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Heterogeneous comparative studies; no numerical effect, bilirubin cutoff, fixed chemotherapy interval, universal metal-design preference or guaranteed freedom from obstruction is inferred.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Only the stated adult clinic consultation and proposed specialist investigations; no acute hypoglycemia rescue or MEN1 operative-extent algorithm is tested.

evidenceClaims.statement: A pancreatic postoperative infected collection often requires antibiotics and effective interventional drainage.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single verified review; source-control approach depends on anatomy and stability. No invented antibiotic regimen.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

evidenceClaims.statement: Reoperation or completion pancreatectomy is generally reserved for failure of conservative/interventional treatment or a complication that requires surgery.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single verified review. Preserve instability, peritonitis and failed-access boundaries.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

evidenceClaims.statement: A convincingly serous cyst causing adjacent-organ compression can warrant resection despite its usually benign behavior.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single directly verified current position paper; asymptomatic size alone does not establish this indication.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

evidenceClaims.statement: A microcystic pancreatic lesion with a central scar supports a serous-cyst phenotype.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Imaging is suggestive rather than definitive histology; atypical lesions need further characterization.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

evidenceClaims.statement: Imaging suggests cyst subtype but cannot establish histology or exclude malignancy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Independently synthesized guideline fact; exact application remains subject to named clinical review.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

evidenceClaims.statement: Pancreatic-remnant surveillance remains indicated after IPMN resection, including noninvasive disease.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Independently synthesized guideline fact; exact application remains subject to named clinical review.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

evidenceClaims.statement: Low-grade dysplasia at an IPMN resection margin does not by itself require completion pancreatectomy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single targeted international guideline; surveillance and individual cancer risk still matter. Exact margin question checked against European 2018 historical guidance, which is not used as a new reusable corpus.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

evidenceClaims.statement: A completely resected MCN without associated pancreatic cancer does not require postoperative cyst surveillance under ACG guidance.
evidenceClaims.limitation: This applies to confirmed completely resected noninvasive MCN, not presumed imaging-only MCN or IPMN.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.
